column1: # C files deliberately kept inside a library that already has a build.zig.
# Enforced by scripts/checks/check_zig_parallel_trees.py, so a port that
# leaves C behind has to say so here instead of leaving a parallel tree.
# A .c under a library's tests/ needs no row: C test fixtures are how the Zig
# is held to the C ABI, and they are deliberately C.

Compile-time conformance TU for the fw_os port contract; a header with no translation unit behind it is never compiled and rots.

The neutral clock-intent port, landed on dev in #693 and carried onto this branch by the zig/dev sync below it. libs/if is migrated here but not on dev, so dev can add C to it without seeing this checker; the row is what the sync owes. Ports with the rest of the if surface.

Emits the NS image's ra8_ns_rot_header_t record; stays C on purpose, as tests/cmake/zig_libraries.cmake records, so the magic word and struct shape are compiler-checked instead of hand-assembled in the NS linker scripts.

column1: # ra8_dfu is partially migrated: the polled USB-DFU host driver is Zig
# (#2809), the boot logic the bootloader runs at reset is Zig (#2918), and
# the root-of-trust verifier is Zig (#2943); four C TUs remain. The two that
# are left of the root-of-trust block (antirollback, launch) are blocked by
# white-box suites that #include the .c files, not by the shared trailer
# record; #2932 has the reading and the porting order.

column3: USBX DFU device class bound to real MRAM through the ux_dcd_ra8_usb bridge. Its seam is the vendored USBX callback surface rather than ra8_usb_host_*, so it ports after the host side proves the pattern (#2809).

Board boot path, kept C in #2987 and ported as its own slice. ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. Nothing in the host gates sees a section placement or a weak override, so an ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.

column1: # ra8_board_ek_ra8d2 is the first PARTIALLY ported board (#2998): the dual-core
# shared-RAM descriptor, the USB full-speed port routing, the board bringup
# sequence, the VCOM console stream and the clock-profile binding are Zig, and
# their C is deleted. Everything below is the C that has NOT moved yet, with
# the reason it has not. Unlike ra8_board_ra8p1 this board keeps its
# src/ra8_board_<board>.c, which is exactly what tells sources.cmake the flip
# is partial and the Zig archive links beside the remaining objects.

column3: The board core: pin tables, LED and switch wiring, clock init and the board-info record, 809 lines and the largest single TU on the board. Its presence is also what tells cmake/ra8_app/sources.cmake this board is only partway flipped (#2998), so it ports last, as the slice that completes the board.

J32 MIPI-DSI panel bring-up, all that is left of the old comms unit after #3003 moved the board clock init and the VCOM console to Zig. It instantiates ra8_mipi_dsi_config_t and ra8_mipi_phy_config_t, 308 and 345 lines of type definitions with nested timing and timeout blocks, and nothing available here would catch a mirrored-layout mismatch: no host suite reads the config back, the one suite on this path drives the real HAL against fake MMIO at the register level, and only an ARM link verifies the layout. A silent mismatch mis-programs the D-PHY PLL. Ports when the structs can be read rather than mirrored, or alongside a suite that reads back what was programmed.

USB audio class bound to the vendored USBX callback surface, 960 lines. Same blocker as ra8_dfu/src/ra8_dfu_device.c: the seam is USBX's own callbacks, and @cImport cannot read the vendored headers (they are C23, see #858). Ports after the USBX pattern is proven.
PDM microphone channel setup, 94 lines of register writes with no host suite behind it (#2998).

Board boot path on the first PARTIALLY ported board (#2998). ra8_add_app selects these by filename out of src/boot/ (an app-local override wins, and this board carries ns_usb_handoff and secure_only profiles as well as the default), and the linker script places them; the vector table is a table of weak aliases the image overrides, and system_init runs before anything the host suites can call. tests/cmake/library_sources.cmake globs src/*.c only, so no host suite compiles src/boot at all. An ARM link is the only thing that would verify a port of them.
